segments.text: A food app says its average delivery time is thirty-two minutes.
segments.caption: A food app says its average delivery time is 32 minutes.

segments.text: But it only checked a hundred orders. How sure can it be?
segments.caption: But it only checked 100 orders. How sure can it be?

segments.text: A confidence interval answers that.
segments.caption: A confidence interval answers that.

segments.text: Here's the definition, in simple words.
segments.caption: Here's the definition, in simple words.

segments.text: A confidence interval is a range of values that likely contains the true average.
segments.caption: A confidence interval is a range of values that likely contains the true average.

segments.text: Instead of one number, you give a range: thirty to thirty-four minutes.
segments.caption: Instead of one number, you give a range: 30 to 34 minutes.

segments.text: And a confidence level, like ninety-five percent, tells you how reliable that range is.
segments.caption: And a confidence level, like 95%, tells you how reliable that range is.

segments.text: Why a range? Because every sample gives a slightly different average.
segments.caption: Why a range? Because every sample gives a slightly different average.

segments.text: Check another hundred orders, and you might get thirty-one, or thirty-three and a half.
segments.caption: Check another 100 orders, and you might get 31, or 33.5.

segments.text: One number alone hides that wobble.
segments.caption: One number alone hides that wobble.

segments.text: The range is the sample average, plus or minus a margin of error.
segments.caption: The range is the sample average, plus or minus a margin of error.

segments.text: First, the standard error: the spread of the data, divided by the square root of the sample size.
segments.caption: First, the standard error: the spread of the data, divided by the square root of the sample size.

segments.text: Here, the spread is ten minutes, and the square root of a hundred is ten. So the standard error is one minute.
segments.caption: Here, the spread is 10 minutes, and the square root of 100 is 10. So the standard error is 1 minute.

segments.text: For ninety-five percent, go about two standard errors each way: thirty-two, plus or minus two.
segments.caption: For 95%, go about two standard errors each way: 32, plus or minus 2.

segments.text: Now the tricky part: what does ninety-five percent really mean?
segments.caption: Now the tricky part: what does 95% really mean?

segments.text: It does not mean a ninety-five percent chance that the true average is in this one range.
segments.caption: It does not mean a 95% chance that the true average is in this one range.

segments.text: It means: repeat the survey many times, and about ninety-five out of a hundred ranges will catch the true average.
segments.caption: It means: repeat the survey many times, and about 95 out of 100 ranges will catch the true average.

segments.text: Want a narrower range? Collect more data.
segments.caption: Want a narrower range? Collect more data.

segments.text: Four times the orders, four hundred, cuts the margin in half: thirty-two, plus or minus one.
segments.caption: Four times the orders, 400, cuts the margin in half: 32, plus or minus 1.

segments.text: And with only twenty-five orders, we use the t-distribution, so the range gets wider: about twenty-eight to thirty-six.
segments.caption: And with only 25 orders, we use the t-distribution, so the range gets wider: about 28 to 36.

segments.text: So remember: a confidence interval is a range that likely contains the true value.
segments.caption: So remember: a confidence interval is a range that likely contains the true value.

segments.text: Average, plus or minus a margin. More data, narrower range.
segments.caption: Average, plus or minus a margin. More data, narrower range.

segments.text: Quick quiz!
segments.caption: Quick quiz!

segments.text: A survey of a hundred people has a margin of error of four points.
segments.caption: A survey of 100 people has a margin of error of 4 points.

segments.text: If you survey four hundred people instead, what's the new margin?
segments.caption: If you survey 400 people instead, what's the new margin?

segments.text: Two points!
segments.caption: 2 points!

segments.text: Four times the data halves the margin, because the square root of four is two.
segments.caption: Four times the data halves the margin, because the square root of four is two.
